Funding for veteran services, mental health support, and active-duty resources has been slashed, leaving those who serve to fend for themselves. Workers across industries face stagnating wages and vanishing protections as labor budgets are gutted, forcing families into poverty while corporate profits soar. Education, the cornerstone of an informed democracy, is crumbling; schools lack resources, teachers are underpaid, and students are left behind in overcrowded classrooms.

A nation that cannot care for its people is no democracy at all—it’s a hollow shell, ruled by those who profit from our suffering.

Democracy dies in darkness, but it thrives in the streets, in the voices of the united, in the courage of those who show up. We must take our fight offline, where real change is forged. Join us in a nationwide protest to demand an end to these devastating cuts and a return to a government that serves its people.
The United States, once a beacon of democratic ideals, is crumbling under the weight of relentless cuts that gut the very systems we rely on—our military personnel, workers, medical care, and education. These slashes aren't just budget adjustments; they’re a deliberate attack on the backbone of our society, eroding the foundations of a free and fair nation. Before the government can detain people pretrial, state and federal law require that pretrial defendants have an evidentiary hearing with the assistance of defense counsel. Hamilton County deprives many pretrial defendants of these rights.

Court Watch is essential in our campaign to end these unconstitutional bail practices.

Our goal is to identify cases where judges set pretrial restrictions like bond. Since magistrate hearings are not public, we observe General Sessions Court during defendants' first appearances. By coordinating with local defense attorneys, we aim to witness more bond hearings and document practices that violate defendants' constitutional rights.

Join Hope In Action (HIA) for a community event honoring the legacy of the Tulsa Massacre and affirming that hope is revolutionary in the face of historical and ongoing racial violence.

 We remember. We organize. We give back.

We will be peacefully protesting and giving back to the community through mutual aid.

Collecting monetary donations — all going directly to support the NAACP’s local racial justice efforts.

Let’s make memory active. Let’s turn mourning into movement.
Because remembrance without resistance is not enough.
